original_description: Keep THIS repository's knowledge plane (the AgentsFramework `agent` monorepo: `docs/` + root `research/`, organized as OKF bundles, governed by `docs/CONVENTIONS_OKF.md` and linted by `scripts/okf_lint.py`) in sync with the actual code and pipeline. This is the skill for ANY work that documents, records, organizes, or freshens the repo's written knowledge after something changes. Use it whenever the user wants to: document or capture a shipped feature/fix/pipeline change as a recipe ("we just wired up X, write it up", "add a runbook for the new deploy step", "capture the carrier-gate shadow audit", "document the memory soft-suppress feature"); write up or record EVAL / TRACE-AUDIT / MEMORY work as durable docs (a probe rubric, a trace-audit finding, a memory-tuning decision) — the WRITING/recording of it lives here even when the underlying work is evaluation, telemetry, or runtime memory; file or organize research and design notes so they stay findable; refresh ANY stale doc against the code, including architecture docs, the planning docs, or the root README ("is our doc knowledge stale vs the code?", "update the README with the new test counts", "make sure the architecture docs reflect the new planner behavior"); or get the docs tree typed, catalogued, and passing the OKF lint gate ("bring docs/explainability up to the convention", "make the recipes tree lint-clean", "move STYLE_GUIDE into a subfolder without breaking the @-mentions"). It writes features up as recipes in the house shape, files research in the right bundle, runs a code↔docs drift check, safely relocates docs with full reference rewriting, and keeps everything lint-green so humans and agents can both extract it — reusing the bundled generator scripts and the repo's `okf_lint.py` gate. Trigger broadly and even when the user never says "OKF", "recipe", "docs", or "frontmatter" — if the intent is to make the repo's written knowledge correct, current, and findable, this is the skill. It does NOT itself run tests, build/ship product code, or answer general questions; it curates the knowledge that records that work.
